manifest.description: Marks (confirmations and flags) and their resolutions for the Curation application
manifest.author: AgenticNetOS

readme:
# Curation

A model that explains something (a product, a process, an organisation, a body of rules, a code base) is only as good as the person's agreement with it. Curation records that agreement, and its absence, on any subject of the Model Explorer:

- `confirm`: the person (or a persona on their behalf) agrees that the subject describes what it claims to describe, at a revision; an optional `sourceHash` records the state of the referenced code at that moment.
- `flag`: the subject is `stale`, `unclear`, `wrong`, a `contradiction`, `unmeasured`, `too-coarse`, or the level below or above changed (`level-below-changed`, `level-above-changed`). A flag stays open until it is resolved.
- `resolve`: how an open flag was settled (the model changed, the person confirmed, the flag was wrong).

Subjects are addressed by `subjectKind` and `subjectKey`: a net `session::net`, an element `session::net#elementId`, a level by its id, a relation `from::net>relation>to::net`. Every write appends one token; the Explorer folds them on read: a subject is `flagged` while any flag is open, `confirmed` when its newest confirmation stands, `unconfirmed` otherwise.

The Explorer shows the state on every band, card and element and offers a filter for what needs the person. The MCP server reads the same fold through `review_model` and writes through `application_action`.
